review_method: Root read complete MainLemma source and lower-level modules, then compared only the accepted opening229-247 declarations against other accepted APIs. Both mathematical facts/proof mechanisms are explicit per row. Later MainLemma declarations are not assessed by this preparation.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: The completed MainLemma opening fixes analytic parameters/coefficient cutoffs, bounds univariate polynomial remainder growth and describes/counts a bounded integer polynomial family. HasseDeriv establishes exact divided differential operators and binomial identities. A degree-box domain for future derivative constraints is not itself a derivative formula; scalar log/floor or remainder bounds need no chosen Hasse order.
blocks.default_action: Retain parameter, remainder and finite-family APIs separately from characteristic-safe differential algebra; share only the actual exponent/support ingredients.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Taylor handles exact shift/substitution, coefficients and polynomial reconstruction. The accepted MainLemma opening has no derivative-index construction yet: it proves analytic budgets, division coefficient estimates and finite family counts. Polynomial coefficient-array reconstruction in boxFamily is at the origin and counts independent integral choices, not inverse translation at an arbitrary point.
blocks.default_action: Keep translation identities separate from scalar budgets and bounded coefficient-family representation; use generic coefficient extensionality where shared.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: CoeffNorm controls l1 sums, derivatives, diagonalization, evaluation and determinants of integer multivariate polynomials. The general remainder theorem instead iterates leading-term cancellation in univariate polynomial division over a seminormed ring, including nonmonic/zero-divisor unchanged-remainder cases. Its coefficient bounds may later receive derivative/diagonal estimates as inputs; that application does not identify the operations or prove division-growth control.
blocks.default_action: Coordinate coefficient magnitude envelopes and triangle inequalities while retaining the distinct derivative/diagonal/evaluation and division-growth estimates.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: The accepted MainLemma opening constructs numerical budgets and finite polynomial choices, while Wronskian studies univariate derivative determinants and linear independence. Both use natural polynomial degrees or finite products, but a cardinality inequality or norm bound cannot replace Vandermonde nonvanishing, and determinant nonvanishing supplies no chosen coefficient cutoff.
blocks.default_action: Keep the two construction stages distinct and share only applicable generic finite-product/degree infrastructure.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Generalized Wronskians use bounded-degree substitution and differential spans to select nonzero determinants. The completed MainLemma opening constructs many bounded-coefficient polynomials and scalar estimates for a later pigeonhole argument. Existence of a nonzero row selection for independent columns is not a count of coefficient choices, and finite coefficient-family size says nothing about independence of a chosen family.
blocks.default_action: Retain finite candidate enumeration and differential determinant selection as separate layers.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Separation extracts variable blocks, chooses a coefficient-span basis and descends rational factors integrally with degree control. MainLemma's completed opening bounds arbitrary polynomial remainder coefficients and represents/counts a finite coefficient box. Monic division and primitive factor descent are different algebraic operations; one controls growth after subtraction, the other rescales exact nonzero products and preserves their degrees.
blocks.default_action: Keep generic remainder growth separate from separated-factor construction and arithmetic normalization.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Index calculates local weighted vanishing for one polynomial through translated support minima. The currently accepted MainLemma opening does not yet prove its later index certificate: gamma/eta are chosen thresholds, remainder bounds and box counts prepare constraints. A numerical threshold definition is not proof that a polynomial attains that order.
blocks.default_action: Retain local-order calculus separately from analytic parameter choice and finite candidate preparation; do not mark later index constructions complete.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Theta proves uniform upper bounds on weighted vanishing at rational points through determinant estimates and dimension induction. MainLemma's completed opening chooses lambda/gamma/eta/coefficient budgets, bounds division growth and counts candidate polynomials. These align the later contradiction budgets but do not themselves prove Theta's upper bound or construct the high-index/nonvanishing auxiliary polynomial. Similar log/power absorption subproofs should share generic monotonicity rather than be treated as identical full formulas.
blocks.default_action: Coordinate scalar budget lemmas and actual height/index inputs; keep supremum upper bounds, parameter existence and coefficient-family counting as distinct mathematical content.

special_pairs.comparison: eta names the explicit real number10^m times delta to the iterated half-power. Theta_lt proves an admissible-family supremum is strictly below that expression under degree-ratio and logarithmic denominator hypotheses. Naming the bound does not prove the estimate.
special_pairs.action: Retain a local descriptive bound alias only if useful; preserve the substantive extremal theorem and its full hypotheses.

special_pairs.comparison: Small-delta existence uses continuity at0 and m>16n^2 to make eta less than gamma. Theta_lt bounds a different supremum by eta given denominator/degree balance. One supplies a parameter gap and the other the pointwise arithmetic upper estimate needed later.
special_pairs.action: Keep analytic parameter existence and uniform index estimate separate; assemble the gap in the application.

special_pairs.comparison: eta_lt_gam_iff is linear rearrangement after unfolding explicit loss definitions. Lemma7 numeric propagates an upper bound on Phi through a nonlinear square-root expression. A shared appearance of a half-power does not identify the arithmetic statements.
special_pairs.action: Use generic linear normalization for the equivalence, retaining the separate nonlinear recurrence estimate.

special_pairs.comparison: Both absorb concrete products into a denominator real power using logarithmic budgets. Their factors differ: the MainLemma triple handles derivative/diagonal/remainder growth, whereas lem6M_lt handles factorial/dimension factors and a scaled coefficient cutoff. A generic positive-product log-budget or rpow monotonicity lemma may package the common final comparison, but not their distinct factor estimates.
special_pairs.action: Consider sharing the proven scalar absorption primitive after inspecting exact positivity and exponent budgets; retain the independent estimates of each product's factors.

special_pairs.comparison: Both prove exponential absorption from a logarithmic lower budget. The first concludes2<q^delta from a squared-delta condition; the second absorbs a natural power-of-two loss into a different rpow with degree/size factors. Shared log monotonicity does not erase the different exponent normalizations or auxiliary factor bounds.
special_pairs.action: Factor only a genuinely identical generic log-to-rpow comparison if justified; keep the current numerical hypothesis conversions separate.

special_pairs.comparison: Diagonal coefficient bounds account for merging several multivariate monomials to the same total exponent. Remainder bounds account for successive leading-term cancellations under division and exponential inflation by the divisor coefficient bound. Either bound can feed the other, but their amplification mechanisms differ.
special_pairs.action: Keep both generic coefficient estimates and compose them in the remainder application.

special_pairs.comparison: The remainder induction uses coefficientwise norm_sub_le over a seminormed ring; normOne_add_le bounds an l1 sum over all integer multivariate coefficients. A norm on one coefficient and an l1 polynomial norm are different objects, despite both using triangle inequalities.
special_pairs.action: Share existing norm triangle primitives, retaining univariate division descent and multivariate l1 aggregation separately.

special_pairs.comparison: boxFamily permits zero and requires every integer coefficient in[0,B]. RSet requires a nonzero polynomial with coefficients bounded in absolute value. Taking the difference of distinct box members yields an RSet member with boundB rather than2B; the two sets are not equal.
special_pairs.action: Preserve the nonnegative candidate family separately from the nonzero symmetric admissible family; connect them by the difference theorem when assessed.

special_pairs.comparison: Finiteness of the bounded nonnegative coefficient family uses finite degree support. Admissibility of polynomial1 in the symmetric nonzero family requires B>=1 and no enumeration. One property does not provide the other family's membership witness.
special_pairs.action: Keep finite candidate enumeration separate from a unit admissibility witness.

special_pairs.comparison: Exact cardinality counts bounded coefficient assignments. Index-set nonemptiness constructs a polynomial/rational-point witness and its scalar index. Even a nonempty candidate box contains zero and does not automatically supply an admissible nonzero symmetric-family witness for B<1.
special_pairs.action: Preserve the different families and coefficient-threshold requirements.

special_pairs.comparison: The count estimate uses the upper floor bound and rpow superadditivity to obtain a strict exponential majorant. The residual-sum estimate lower-bounds a finite positive-part sum by a quadratic floor expression. Both contain natural floors but use different inequality directions and summands.
special_pairs.action: Share floor primitives, retain scalar count absorption and residual-sum lower bounds as distinct numerical results.
